x: Into the bell in the 1500m and they've shed the pacemaker, Stu' Paton (entry fee sponsored by Oliver Foote to set up a sub 4!) Mark Sinclair looks a picture of relaxation and goes on to a sixth successive win. The next three hung on for pb's - Olly, Frank Ward (behind Mark) and John Booth in his seasonal debut after injury!

Frank Ward also showed that he intends to remain in the "A" team. We did have some good cheer when we collected our Silver team medals but we were lucky because if Olly or David had dropped out we would not have finished in the frame.

BELGRAVE CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIPS 1987.
Frank Ward(8) Winner of 10 Miles Senior, Martin Lake Runner Up in both 7½ and 10 Miles Senior races and Richard Blick (2) Winner of Youths race and Matthew Egerickx(7) Winner of the Boys Championship.
5000 METRES - 15 JUNE: Marcello Bizio quickly took Nigel Clark clear of John Mather and Don Anderson while Frank Ward dawdled through the opening laps at the rear of the field.
The 1988 Championship 5 3/4 was won by Frank Ward - whose main problem appeared to be in following the correct route. Soon after leaving the common, Frank and runner-up Marcello went off course.
On behalf of the members I would like to thank all those who give financial support to the Club, however small or large. Frank Ward
Apart from a fine win by Gary Staines at Wimbledon and an excellent series of races by Frank Ward who finished in 4th place overall, Belgrave lacked support from the better athletes.
The highlight of this low key part one of the Surrey Track and Field Championships was Frank Ward's bronze medal in the 10,000 metres with Roger Alsop in 6th place passing the '5000' mark in a pb.
He took the A race comfortably in the first two BAL 5000m races, backed up well by Frank Ward (2), also shown left, in match 1 and Ollie Foote in match 2.
Congratulations to Cliff Brooks and Doug Fotheringham who were elected Life Members at the recent AGM. And also to Sue Porter, Frank Ward and Keith Duckett, now Vice-Presidents.

Frank Ward did well to finish 3rd in the 5000m and as temperatures soared to the highest of the summer so far, Ollie Foote showed great judgement to gradually pick off all the opposition and sprint home a clear winner in the 10,000m, running a 62 second last lap.
